title: Rapidity-Coupled Spin Dynamics in Pulsed Laser Fields from Physics-Informed Neural Networks
authors: N. S. Akintsov, A. P. Nevecheria, S. N. Andreev, Qing-Hua Qin
abstract: Carrier-envelope-phase (CEP) stabilized few-cycle pulses make the sub-cycle field structure a control parameter for laser-driven polarized electron sources, yet spin solvers for such pulses are rarely tested against exact results. We show that for an electron initially at rest in a linearly polarized plane-wave pulse the rest-frame polarization angle follows the instantaneous vector potential, $Σ= 2\arctan(a_x/2) + a_e a_x$ with $a_e$ the electron anomaly: the net rotation vanishes for every CEP, while the peak intra-pulse angle varies over the CEP by 3.02 degrees for a two-cycle and by 0.22 degrees for an eight-cycle pulse. The result follows from the Volkov orbit in longitudinal and transverse rapidities. We use it to validate a light-front reference integrator and a physics-informed neural network trained only on the light-front equations, which reaches $4\times10^{-5}$ in the spin sector and carries over to elliptical polarization, for which no closed-form solution is known. This gives validated tools for CEP-resolved spin dynamics in intense fields.
summary: This work investigates how the spin of an electron evolves when driven by intense, short laser pulses, focusing on the role of the Carrier-Envelope-Phase (CEP). The authors use a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to solve the complex coupled equations, achieving high accuracy and extending the analysis to elliptical polarization where analytical solutions fail. This provides validated, powerful tools for studying CEP-resolved spin dynamics in extreme electromagnetic fields.
main_problem: Characterizing the spin dynamics of an electron driven by intense, few-cycle, laser pulses, particularly resolving the dependence on the Carrier-Envelope-Phase (CEP).
main_result: The CEP strongly controls the transient intra-pulse polarization angle, though the net spin rotation vanishes for linear polarization. A Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) successfully validates the dynamics, extending to elliptical polarization where no closed-form solution exists.
method: The authors employed advanced numerical techniques, including light-front parameterization, high-order integrators (Dormand-Prince), and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) trained on the governing light-front equations.
model_or_system: The system models a relativistic electron interacting with a plane-wave, few-cycle laser pulse. The dynamics are governed by the coupled equations for the electron's orbital motion and its spin evolution (BMT equation).
key_observables: Rest-frame polarization angle ($\Sigma$), peak intra-pulse angle ($\Sigma_{\max}$), net spin rotation, and peak kinetic energy spread.
important_parameters: Carrier-Envelope-Phase (CEP, $\phi_0$), pulse duration (2-cycle vs. 8-cycle), and the electron's anomalous magnetic moment ($a_e$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes an ideal plane-wave pulse, which leads to the vanishing net spin rotation, suggesting external effects are needed to observe CEP-dependent net polarization changes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the CEP dependence of the polarization angle, showing a significant collapse in the peak angle spread ($\Delta\Sigma_{\max}$) when moving from two-cycle to eight-cycle pulses. Comparisons are made between PINN results and established reference solvers.
paper_structure: The paper develops the exact light-front solution for spin evolution, derives the closed-form expression for linear polarization, and then applies this framework to validate a PINN implementation. The PINN is trained to solve the coupled orbital and spin equations, demonstrating accuracy across various polarization regimes.
why_interesting: The combination of relativistic quantum electrodynamics (BMT equation) with modern machine learning tools (PINNs) to solve complex, non-linear, time-dependent physics problems is highly relevant for developing next-generation computational physics tools.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Carrier-envelope-phase control of the intra-pulse spin dynamics for an electron initially at rest in a cos2-envelope pulse with a0 = 0.42. (a) Normalized vector potential ax(η) (grey) and the rest-frame polarization angle Σ(η) for φ0 = 0 and φ0 = π/2 in a two-cycle pulse; Σ = 2 arctan(ax/2)+aeax. (b) Peak angle Σmax = maxη |Σ| versus CEP for N = 2 and N = 8 cycles; the CEP-induced spread collapses from 3.02◦to 0.22◦as the pulse lengthens. (c) Peak kinetic energy γmax−1, normalized to its CEP average, showing a 26.6% spread for N = 2 against 1.90% for N = 8; γmax −1 = a2 max/2 exactly, with amax = maxη |ax|. In all cases the net rotation after the pulse vanishes, Eq. (6).

FIG. 2. Physics-informed neural network solution of the light- front orbital and BMT equations, Eq. (3) with d/dτ = κ d/dη, for a0 = 0.42, N = 2, φ0 = 0.7 rad. (a) Lorentz factor γ(η) from the PINN (dashed) against the Dormand–Prince refer- ence (solid). (b) Components of the spin four-vector Sµ(η), same convention. (c) Maximum relative error at the end of the pulse versus fixed step budget for a co-propagating elec- tron (κ = 0.050), comparing lab-time Runge–Kutta, the Boris and Higuera–Cary pushers (both with a Cayley spin update) and the light-front rapidity parameterization. (d) Pointwise absolute error of the trained network against the reference, |∆γ| and maxµ |∆Sµ|, over the pulse.
